attack_1_same_path.detail: YES, verified two ways. Code: arms set JEV_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPT=2 inline on out=$(... run) and run() execs $LS in-shell, so the env propagates (bash function env inheritance). Fixtures match my runs shape-for-shape (stable clean/drifted STATUS + real sidecar + JEV_STATUS). Live: full suite green 17/17 at target, arms 15/16 PASS. RESIDUAL: my runs HEAD-bracketed; arms do not — a concurrent lane commit mid-arm drives attempt-2 to rc=10 and FAILS the arm spuriously. Windows are ~1s in a lane committing every few minutes: rare, real, and indistinguishable from a true failure without bracketing. Recommend HEAD-bracket or known-flake note.

attack_2_copy_vs_pattern.detail: REAL DEFECT, bounded. ARM 17 feeds a HAND-WRITTEN line through a HAND-COPIED sed. If lane-status.sh's sed changes again, the arm keeps passing on its frozen pair while production diverges — the stale-assertion class one level up (b031ffb's defect was an un-re-run assertion; this is an assertion that CANNOT observe the next change). Mitigating: I just proved end-to-end naming live at HEAD (bounded drip -> rc=10, 'Changed paths: /tmp/tr/mut3.json', HEAD-bracketed stable), so the defect is latent, not live. Honest form: extract the sed EXPRESSION from lane-status.sh at test time and apply it to the hand-written fixture line — a format change then FAILS the arm until a human updates the fixture, which is exactly the forced re-examination the defect class demands.

attack_3_anchoring.detail: SOUND for all realistic inputs. Both verdict prints start at column 0 (leading \n only); every other output line is indented (rows two-space, commit block sed-prefixed two-space, extracted paths re-indented two-space, candidate names field-padded). The cccaf39-subject collision that motivated it cannot recur through these predicates. Residual: a newline embedded in a tracked path could inject a column-0 line — pathological, unobserved in this tree, stated not pursued.
